➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

Cisco Expressway Series Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-vcs-static-cred-hr7EWZ8t?vs_f=Cisco%20Security%20Advisory%26vs_cat=Security%20Intelligence%26vs_type=RSS%26vs_p=Cisco%20Expressway%20Series%20Remote%20Code%20Execution%20Vulnerability%26vs_k=1

A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to a Cisco Expressway device to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root.
This vulnerability is due to the use of persistent cookies. Additionally, there is insufficient validation of client certificates when the TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, which means that client certificates are not validated. An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device.
Note: Cisco Expressway Series refers to Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) devices and Cisco Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices.

Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability.
This advisory is available at the following link:
https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-vcs-static-cred-hr7EWZ8t
This advisory is part of a group of advisories. Some very troubling U.S. inflation data was released recently. PPI rose 6.3% year over year, versus expectations of 5.5%, and jumped 1.3% month over month, compared with forecasts of 0.6%. That’s the biggest monthly increase in producer prices since March 2022.

PPI shows how prices are changing for businesses themselves. When production, energy, transportation, and other costs go up, some of those increases are usually passed on to consumers over time. On top of that, the previous day’s consumer inflation report also came in hotter than expected. In other words, there have now been two consecutive signals that the U.S. inflation problem isn’t going away.

This is bad news for markets for a very simple reason. The higher inflation is, the less room the Fed has to cut rates, and the more likely interest rates are to stay elevated for longer. High rates are particularly painful for tech companies, crypto, and other assets that depend more heavily on cheap money and liquidity.

Part of the recent spike is indeed tied to energy prices, which jumped 10.8% in a single month. So it’s too early to call this a new inflation crisis based on one data point. But the problem is that price increases are showing up in other areas too, which means it’s not possible to blame everything on oil alone.

For Bitcoin over the long term, a single report doesn’t fundamentally change anything. But over the next few weeks, data like this increases the likelihood of pressure across the broader crypto market. The same goes for stocks, especially tech stocks.

That’s why it’s best not to rush into buying every dip right now. It makes more sense to keep some capital in cash and be prepared to buy quality assets at lower prices if the pressure continues. The long-term thesis remains unchanged, but in the short term, the market has one more reason to move lower.
